On this page

Configuration ​

Resrv splits its configuration between two owners, and it helps to know which is which before you start:

  • CP-managed settings: business information, the reservation engine, checkout, emails, and currency. You edit these in the Control Panel under Resrv → Settings, and Statamic stores them on your site at resources/addons/statamic-resrv.yaml. Commit that file to version control.
  • Developer keys: the payment gateway(s), Stripe credentials, and the nested checkout-form / reservation-email override structures. These live in the publishable config/resrv-config.php file.

At boot, Resrv merges all three layers (blueprint defaults, then config/resrv-config.php, then your CP-saved values) into a single resrv-config.* config. The order matters: the Control Panel value always wins over the same key defined in the config file.

Migrating from v5

In v5 every setting lived in config/resrv-config.php. In v6 the business and engine settings moved to the Control Panel. If you are upgrading, run php please resrv:settings:migrate to move your existing values across, see Migrating from a published config below and the upgrade guide.

Settings reference ​

Open Resrv → Settings in the Control Panel. The settings are organised into five tabs: General, Engine, Checkout, Emails, and Currency.

General ​

Business information that is used in the reservation email templates.

FieldDefaultDescription
Business nameResrvYour business name.
Business addressSomestreet 8Street address.
ZIP & City00000 CityZIP code and city.
CountryGreeceCountry.
Phone+30 0000 000000Contact phone.
Emailresrv@resrv.appContact email.
Logo(empty)Leave empty to use your business name, or enter an absolute URL (including https://) to an image.

The Logo field now works

In v6 the Logo field is functional. Paste an absolute https://… URL and the email header renders it automatically as an image. No template editing required. Leave it empty to fall back to your business name. See Emails for details.

Engine ​

Controls how the reservation engine behaves.

FieldDefaultDescription
Enable timefalseRequire an explicit pick-up and drop-off time for each reservation. Not yet implemented in the frontend.
Enable affiliatestrueEnable the affiliate system. Also controls whether the Affiliates nav item appears.
Enable cutoff rulesfalseEnable per-entry cutoff times based on starting times and schedules.
Minimum days before0Minimum number of days allowed between today and the reservation start date. Useful to block last-minute bookings.
Minimum reservation period (in days)1Minimum number of days a reservation must span.
Maximum reservation period (in days)30Maximum number of days a reservation may span.
Free cancellation (in days)0Days before the start date the customer may cancel. Cancellations are manual; this drives the displayed cancellation label.
Require full payment if free cancellation has passedfalseRequire full payment when the free-cancellation window has already passed at booking time.
Maximum quantity8Maximum quantity allowed in one reservation.
Ignore quantity for pricesfalseTrack quantity without multiplying the price by it (e.g. seats at a restaurant).
Calculate days using timefalseWith Enable time, charge an extra day when the return time is after the start time. Not yet implemented in the frontend.
Decrease availability for extra timefalseBlock the final day's availability when the return time is after the start time.
Admin email(empty)Comma-separated list of emails notified about new reservations and refunds. Leave empty to disable admin notifications.

Cancellation policy is now per-rate

Free cancellation (in days) and Require full payment if free cancellation has passed are now the fallback used when a rate has no explicit policy of its own. Each rate can declare its own free-cancellation window or be marked non-refundable. See Rates → Cancellation policy. Non-refundable bookings always require full payment at checkout.

Checkout ​

Controls the checkout process and which form each reservation uses. See the Checkout page for the full flow.

FieldDefaultDescription
Default checkout form(none)The form used when no entry-specific or collection-specific mapping matches. Required.
Collection checkout form mappings(none)Map collection handles to checkout forms. Each row has a Collection (handle, e.g. pages) and a Form.
Entry checkout form mappings(none)Map specific entries to checkout forms. Entry mappings take precedence over collection mappings.
Checkout Entry(none)The Statamic entry that loads the Livewire checkout component. Required.
Checkout Redirect Entry(none)The checkout complete page that includes the resrv_checkout_redirect tag. Required.
Payment typefullWhat the customer pays online to complete a reservation (see below).
Fixed amount50The amount charged. Shown only when Payment type is Charge a fixed amount.
Percentage20The percentage of the base price charged. Shown only when Payment type is Charge a percentage of the base price.
Minutes to hold10How long availability is temporarily blocked when a customer starts checkout, to prevent double bookings.

Payment type options:

ValueCharges
fullThe whole reservation amount.
everythingThe whole amount plus any options and extras.
fixedA fixed amount.
percentA percentage of the base price.

Checkout form mappings ​

Resrv picks the checkout form for a reservation in this order of precedence:

  1. Entry mapping: a form mapped to that specific entry.
  2. Collection mapping: a form mapped to the entry's collection.
  3. Default checkout form: the fallback used when nothing else matches.

You can configure all three from this tab. Developers who prefer to keep the mapping under version control can set the nested checkout_forms array in config/resrv-config.php instead, see Developer config. The deeper walkthrough lives on the Checkout page.

Emails ​

Resrv sends event-based emails (customer confirmation, admin notification, refund, and abandoned-reservation recovery), and you can customise them per event or per checkout form from this tab.

  • Global email event settings: add a row per event to set recipient sources (customer, admins, affiliate), extra email addresses, the From address/name, subject, and template.
  • Per-form email event overrides: override a specific event for a specific checkout form (form overrides win over global, which win over the built-in defaults).
  • Abandoned reservation emails: enable recovery emails for customers who started but did not complete a reservation, and set how many days to wait after the reservation expires.

This tab is described in full on the Emails page, including recipient resolution and the template picker. Do not duplicate it here.

FieldDefaultDescription
Enable abandoned reservation emailsfalseWhen enabled, the resrv:send-abandoned-emails command sends recovery emails to customers with expired reservations.
Delay (in days)1Days after a reservation expires before the recovery email is sent (1 = next day).

Choosing a template

The email Template field is a dropdown that auto-populates from the available templates. To add a custom one, publish the email views (--tag=resrv-emails) and drop a Blade file into resources/views/vendor/statamic-resrv/email/reservations/; it then appears in the dropdown. See Emails.

Developer config ​

The following developer-only keys live in config/resrv-config.php. Publish the file with:

bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=resrv-config
KeyDescription
payment_gatewayThe single payment gateway class. Defaults to StripePaymentGateway. See Payment gateways.
payment_gatewaysOptional array of multiple gateways the customer can choose between at checkout. See Payment gateways.
stripe_secret_keyStripe secret key (RESRV_STRIPE_SECRET env). See Stripe.
stripe_publishable_keyStripe publishable key (RESRV_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE env).
stripe_webhook_secretStripe webhook signing secret (RESRV_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET env).
checkout_formsNested default / collections / entries override of the CP checkout-form mappings.
reservation_emailsNested global / forms override of the CP email settings.

Nested overrides win

The nested checkout_forms and reservation_emails arrays take precedence over their flat CP counterparts when set. Use them only if you want the mapping in code under version control, and do not mix nested config with the equivalent CP settings for the same key.

These are the only keys this file should contain. Defining a CP-managed key (business info, engine, currency, etc.) here has no effect once a value exists in the Control Panel: the CP value silently wins.

Migrating from a published config ​

If you are upgrading from v5, your CP-managed settings still live in config/resrv-config.php. Move them into the Control Panel with:

bash
php please resrv:settings:migrate

Add --dry-run to preview the changes without saving anything:

bash
php please resrv:settings:migrate --dry-run

The command:

  • Seeds the CP-managed keys from your published config into the CP settings store. It skips any key that already has a CP value (your saved value always wins), is null, or still equals the blueprint default.
  • Reports conflicts where the file and the CP store disagree (the CP value stays active; the file value is shown for review).
  • Lists keys you can delete from config/resrv-config.php: both the now-CP-managed keys and any stale keys that v6 no longer uses (such as enable_advanced_availability, enable_connected_availabilities, and form_name).
  • Reminds you which developer keys to keep in the file.

When you upgrade to 6.0.0, Resrv runs this migration automatically once. The manual command is for re-running it, previewing with --dry-run, or installs where the automatic step did not fire.

Published config file detected

While config/resrv-config.php still defines CP-managed keys, a warning section titled "⚠ Published config file detected" appears at the top of the General settings tab, listing the affected keys. The CP values override the file at runtime. Remove those keys from the file (or run resrv:settings:migrate) and the banner disappears.

Removed in v6 ​

These v5 config keys no longer do anything and are reported as stale keys by resrv:settings:migrate:

  • enable_advanced_availability: replaced by the collection-scoped Rates system.
  • enable_connected_availabilities: connected availabilities were removed; use Rates instead.
  • form_name: replaced by the checkout form mappings (default / collection / entry).
